title: Lee2021 – SSVEP paradigm of the Mobile BCI dataset
description: This dataset comprises steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) recordings from 23 healthy participants performing a brain-computer interface (BCI) task during various locomotor states (standing, walking, running). The study employed 73-channel EEG acquisition at 100 Hz sampling rate with three visual flicker stimuli at 5.45, 8.57, and 12.0 Hz, collected across 4 sessions per subject. The dataset is designed to evaluate BCI performance in mobile and naturalistic environments.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a 73-channel BrainAmp system (Brain Product GmbH) at 100 Hz sampling rate with Ag/AgCl electrodes referenced to FCz and grounded at Fpz. Impedance was maintained below 50 kOhm. Four additional EOG channels monitored eye movements. Participants performed SSVEP-based BCI tasks during three locomotor conditions (standing, walking, running) with visual stimuli presented at three frequencies (5.45, 8.57, 12.0 Hz). Each trial lasted 5 seconds with 20 trials per class across 4 sessions.
